faq.q: What is the origin of Farokh?
faq.a: Farokh is associated with Persian. Persian farrokh ('happy, auspicious, fortunate'). The source record's gloss 'Lord, Master' is unsupported. The source record classified it as Arabic, which is incorrect.
No — the underlying form is Persian, not Arabic.
Farokh can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Persian-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.

faq.q: What does Farokh mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Farokh is rendered فروخ and carries the sense سرور، خداوند.

faq.a: Romanization variants include Farokh, farokh. Script forms are فروخ, फ़रोख़.

faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
